Three Connect layers — do not merge them

App Store Connect stores language and geography in separate places. English-primary indie apps usually get stuck because one layer looks “done” while another is empty.

1 — Primary Language (app record default)

Set once when you create the app. For most Western indies this is English (U.S.). Primary Language defines which locale Connect treats as the app’s administrative home: default labels in some admin views, the locale teammates see first, and the fallback metadata Apple uses when a buyer’s language row is missing or blank. Primary Language English does not mean China gets English on purpose — it means English is your canonical row until you fill others.

2 — Localization rows (per-locale product copy)

Under the App Store tab, each language is its own row: en-US, Chinese (Simplified) / zh-Hans, and others. Each row holds independent name, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, What’s New, screenshots, and preview assets. Adding zh-Hans creates the row structure; it does not copy or translate your en-US text. Saving Primary Language as English while zh-Hans fields stay empty is a valid Connect state — and a common reason the China storefront shows English.

3 — Storefront availability (download geography)

Pricing and Availability controls which countries and regions can install the app. Checking China makes the app discoverable on the China App Store. It does not insert Chinese characters into any field. Availability answers “can they download?” Localizations answer “what copy do they read?”

All three must align for a finished China presence: China available, zh-Hans row added, and zh-Hans text fields saved (plus zh-Hans screenshots if you want a fully native gallery).

Why English Primary Language confuses China setup

Connect’s UI reinforces the wrong mental model in two ways:

  • Primary Language sounds global. New developers read “primary” as “the language all storefronts use unless I override.” In practice, each storefront pulls from the matching localization row; empty zh-Hans triggers fallback to en-US regardless of what Primary Language says.
  • Adding a locale looks like progress. The language dropdown shows Chinese (Simplified) after you add it — but blank name and description fields still mean “not localized.” Connect does not warn you that storefront availability and Primary Language are already satisfied while zh-Hans copy is not.
  • en-US reads “complete.” Your English row passed review. It is easy to assume the app is “fully listed” while China is technically available but still serving fallback English — because the zh-Hans row was never filled with distinct copy.

You usually do not need to change Primary Language to ship Chinese metadata. Keep English primary if your team, support, and default marketing stay en-US-first. The work is completing the zh-Hans row, not reordering the app record.

Connect checklist — Primary Language vs zh-Hans row

Use this order in App Store Connect before you pay for copy help or switch Primary Language:

  1. Confirm Primary Language — App Information → Primary Language should reflect your real home locale (English for most Western indies). No change required for China if you plan to keep en-US as admin default.
  2. Confirm China availability — Pricing and Availability → China checked. Without this, zh-Hans copy will not surface on the China App Store even when filled.
  3. Open the zh-Hans row — App Store tab → language dropdown → Chinese (Simplified). If missing, add localization — you still need to paste text afterward.
  4. Audit core fields — With zh-Hans selected, verify saved text in name, subtitle, keywords, and description. Placeholder or empty fields mean fallback to en-US on the China storefront.
  5. Match screenshots to locale — zh-Hans screenshot slots are separate per device size. English gallery art with Chinese text (or the reverse) signals an incomplete localization.
  6. Submit metadata changes — Filled rows on a live app still require App Review submission before buyers see updated copy.

When steps 1–2 are green but 3–4 fail, you need zh-Hans copy — not a Primary Language change. AppLocale writes that row from your existing English listing.

FAQ

Does English Primary Language in App Store Connect mean my China listing is in Chinese?

No. Primary Language is the locale you set when creating the app record — usually en-US for Western indie teams. It does not auto-fill a Simplified Chinese (zh-Hans) localization row. China storefront buyers see zh-Hans fields when that row is complete; otherwise Apple falls back to your primary English metadata.

What is the difference between Primary Language, localization rows, and storefront availability?

Primary Language is the app's home locale in Connect admin. Localization rows (en-US, zh-Hans, etc.) hold separate title, subtitle, keywords, and description per language. Storefront availability under Pricing and Availability controls which countries can download — enabling China does not create or translate a zh-Hans row.

I added Chinese (Simplified) in Connect — why is the row still not enough?

Adding zh-Hans creates empty fields. Primary Language staying English is normal and correct for en-US-first apps. The gap is unfilled name, subtitle, keywords, or description in the zh-Hans row — not the primary locale setting itself.

Should I change Primary Language to Chinese for the China storefront?

Almost never for Western indie apps. Switching primary locale is an admin structural move — it does not translate fields and can confuse teammates who work in English. Fill the zh-Hans localization row instead; keep English primary if your operations stay en-US-first.
